newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam sets tight rules for foreign workers.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam sets tight rules for foreign workers.

text.p: Hanoi spelt out new rules on Wednesday for foreigners working in Vietnam, setting time limits on the period they can stay in the country and compelling employers to replace them with trained local staff.

The prime ministerial decree was published in a two-page spread in the English-language Vietnam News, which said foreign residents, including overseas Vietnamese, would require a work permit from March of next year.
The paper said foreigners could only be hired if the necessary know-how was not available locally, and then for a maximum period of three years.
Employers will be required to replace foreign workers with a trained Vietnamese national at the end of their term.
Reaction among local business executives on Wednesday was mixed, with some applauding the move and others expressing concern.
"Other countries have strict labour codes... India and Malaysia for example, but it might be a bit early to apply these here," one said.
Other analysts said the move appeared aimed at shifting governmental control over the growing number of foreigners in Vietnam from the visa-issuing authorities to the Labour Ministry.

Company directors, foreigners employed by the Vietnamese authorities, members of donor or other international organisations and individuals working for news organisations would be exempt from the new regulations.
